heard: A new star once cast shadows across the Earth. It appeared in the sky brighter than the planet Venus. This celestial fire was so intense people saw it during midday. Astronomer Tycho Brahe proved it sat far beyond our moon. That discovery shattered the myth that the heavens never change. Space dust reflected its original light back to us in 2008. This light echo proved a white dwarf, a dead star's core, had exploded. Research suggests the blast inspired a young William Shakespeare. He saw the same ghost star that cast shadows across the Earth.
